question: What is the timeline for diagnosing conjunctivitis as ophthalmia neonatorum in a newborn?

options.A: Within the first 28 days of life
options.B: Within the first week of life only
options.D: During the first 72 hours of life

explanation: Ophthalmia neonatorum is strictly defined as any conjunctivitis affecting an infant during the first 28 days of life, matching the neonatal period. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h1)

question: Why is prompt identification of neonatal conjunctivitis critical in clinical practice?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any systemic antibiotic therapy
options.B: It stops the mother from developing postpartum depression
options.C: It guarantees the infant will not catch common colds
options.D: It prevents rapid progression to corneal scarring and blindness

explanation: Early detection allows for swift intervention, stopping the infection from destroying the delicate corneal tissue and causing irreversible vision loss. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h1)

question: A newborn presents with severe purulent discharge and lid swelling on the third day of life. Which organism is most likely responsible?
explanation: Gonococcal conjunctivitis typically has a very short incubation period of two to four days and presents with copious pus production. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h2)

question: Which clinical feature is most characteristic of gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum?

options.A: Clear watery tears with no swelling
options.C: Small white spots on the iris surface
options.D: Thick, profuse pus that accumulates rapidly

explanation: Gonococcal eye infections produce a uniquely heavy, constant flow of purulent discharge due to intense inflammation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h3)

question: When does chemical conjunctivitis secondary to eye prophylaxis typically appear in a newborn?

options.A: Around the seventh day of postnatal life
options.B: At the end of the first month
options.C: Between the second and third week
options.D: Within hours of birth and drug instillation

explanation: Chemical irritation from prophylactic drops occurs almost immediately after administration and clears up on its own within a short time. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h3)

question: What is the primary diagnostic procedure used to identify the causative organism in eye discharge?

options.A: Ultrasound examination of the orbital socket
options.C: Conjunctival swab for Gram stain and culture
options.D: Complete blood count with differential count

explanation: Swabbing the conjunctiva allows laboratory personnel to grow and identify the exact bacteria causing the infection. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h4)

question: Why is documenting the exact time of symptom onset crucial during a neonatal eye assessment?

options.A: It dictates the required room temperature for the baby
options.B: It determines the exact birth weight of the infant
options.C: It helps differentiate between chemical, gonococcal, and chlamydial causes
options.D: It proves whether the mother attended antenatal care clinics

explanation: Different pathogens have distinct incubation periods, meaning the day symptoms appear gives strong clues about the causative agent. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h4)

question: Why must gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum be treated with systemic antibiotics rather than eye drops alone?

options.A: Newborns cannot absorb any medications through eye tissues
options.B: Topical drops alone cannot prevent systemic invasion and corneal damage
options.C: Systemic drugs are cheaper to purchase in local pharmacies
options.D: Eye drops cause permanent staining of the infant's iris

explanation: Gonococcus can invade the intact corneal epithelium rapidly, requiring systemic coverage in addition to local care to save the eye. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h5)

question: What is a key nursing intervention when caring for a newborn with purulent conjunctivitis?

options.A: Performing frequent saline eye irrigations to remove pus
options.B: Applying tight eye patches to keep light away
options.C: Placing the infant in a dark isolation room
options.D: Withholding all feeds until eye discharge stops

explanation: Washing away built-up purulent discharge prevents it from pooling and allows prescribed topical medications to contact the tissues directly. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h5)

question: Which medication is commonly used for routine eye prophylaxis in newborns?
explanation: Tetracycline ointment is widely applied to newborn eyes immediately after birth to prevent bacterial conjunctivitis. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of administering prophylactic eye ointment to every newborn?

options.A: Preventing blocked tear ducts in the first week
options.B: Preventing ophthalmia neonatorum acquired during birth
options.C: Improving visual acuity in premature infants
options.D: Treating congenital cataracts before they worsen

explanation: Prophylaxis aims to destroy infectious organisms picked up as the baby passes through an infected birth canal. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h6)
